description.text:
The promos of Japan's PCG years: 154 cards, 001/PCG-P to 154/PCG-P, released from February 2004 to July 2006. They began soon after Undone Seal, the last Japanese expansion with the ADV prefix, when the promo suffix changed from ADV-P to PCG-P.

Most came in a few big runs: Meiji Chocolate cards in 2004, 2005 and 2006, McDonald's promotions in 2005 and 2006, the attraction cards of the PokéPark 2005 theme park, and Battle Road prizes every season, from participation cards to finals prizes such as the Holon Energy cards of autumn 2005. Others came with CoroCoro Comic, Shogakukan's elementary school magazines and Pokémon Wonderland, with the film Mew and the Wave Hero: Lucario and the video of Pikachu's Summer Festival, in official card files, deck cases and the Team Rocket Special Boxes, from the Official Pokémon Card Gym lotteries, for Pokémon Center openings, and in All Nippon Airways' Pika Summer Trip of 2006.

description.text: Mitsuhiro Arita's Blastoise came with the March 2004 issue of CoroCoro Comic, published on 15 February 2004, as a card only that magazine gave. It is the first card of the PCG-P promos; Arita's Charizard (002/PCG-P) and Venusaur (003/PCG-P) followed that spring. The same art is on the English Blastoise, No. 1 of POP Series 3, booster packs given out at Pokémon Organized Play events.

Mitsuhiro Arita's Charizard was the participation card of Battle Road Spring 2004: everyone who played in its official tournament got one. The same art is on the English Charizard of EX Dragon (No. 100).

Battle Road Spring 2004 ran regional tournaments across Japan from 21 March to 4 April 2004, in junior, senior and master leagues. Players first battled in a qualifying round, and the top eight of each league went on to the final tournament.

Mitsuhiro Arita's Venusaur was given at the Pokémon Card Game Gym Official events of Sunday 11 and Sunday 18 April 2004, in exchange for a ticket from the April 2004 issue of CoroCoro Comic or the May 2004 issues of Shogakukan's magazines for the first to fourth and sixth grades of elementary school. The announcement called it an original card that could only be had at the event. The same art is on the English Venusaur, No. 6 of POP Series 2, booster packs given out at Pokémon Organized Play events.

The Official Pokémon Card Gyms (ポケモンカードジムオフィシャル) were game and hobby shops across Japan that hosted official play from October 2000.

Ken Sugimori's Ivysaur was won in a lottery held at the Official Pokémon Card Gyms in April 2004 to mark the start of the gyms' season. The same art is on the English Ivysaur, No. 7 of POP Series 2, booster packs given out at Pokémon Organized Play events.

The Official Pokémon Card Gyms (ポケモンカードジムオフィシャル) were game and hobby shops across Japan that hosted official play from October 2000. A lottery at each gym marked the start of the season in 2003 and 2004; Ivysaur was the only card of 2004's, the last one held.

description.text:
Katsura Tabata's Pokémon Card Laboratory was the prize for beating a researcher of the Pokémon Card Laboratory (PCL), the team that makes the game, at the Gym Leader & PCL Challenge corner of Battle Road Summer 2004. Players who beat PCL won it again at the 21st Next Generation World Hobby Fair in January and February 2005 and at Battle Road Summer 2006, where the official report said few players managed it.

The Stadium shows the laboratory, with PCL lab coats and a PCL sign. Once during each player's turn, they may choose a Pokémon card from their hand, say its name and put it face down; the opponent then names one of its attacks. If they are right, the opponent draws a card; if not, the player draws one. The card then goes back to the hand.

Atsuko Nishida's LaRousse's Munchlax, a holo card, marked the reopening of Pokémon Center Tokyo on Tuesday 24 August 2004, after a refit that changed the store's layout. From 24 to 26 August the first 3,000 shoppers at the Pokémon Centers in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Fukuoka and Sapporo got one, as did the first 5,000 buyers from Pokémon Center Online and Pokémon Center Mobile. The announcement called Munchlax the new Pokémon starring in that summer's film, Destiny Deoxys, set in LaRousse City.

Pokumon adds that the card was also given, with Poké Dude, to Pokémon Daisuki Club members who had signed up in advance for the Poké Dude Trainer Exercise on the club's stage at Pokémon Festa 2004.

Another LaRousse's Munchlax by Nishida, with the same attacks and a different picture, came with Shogakukan's grade magazines as 020/PCG-P.

Ryo Ueda's Rocket's Raikou ex was the participation card of Battle Road Autumn 2004: everyone who played in the qualifying round of its official tournament got one. It is non-holo, with the event's logo, バトルロード オータム★2004, stamped in gold on the art. The holo copy without the stamp is 035/PCG-P, from the Team Rocket Special Box. The same art is on the English Rocket's Raikou ex of EX Deoxys (No. 108).

Battle Road Autumn 2004 was held in Osaka on 24 October, Tokyo on 7 November and Nagoya on 21 November 2004, in a junior league and a senior and master league. Each player played seven qualifying games, and the top 16 of each league went on to the final tournament.

description.text: Yuka Morii's Treecko marked the opening of Pokémon Center Yokohama in Landmark Plaza, Minato Mirai, on Saturday 5 March 2005. That day every Pokémon Center, the new store and those in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Fukuoka, gave this original card to its first 10,000 visitors. In its art Treecko stands in front of a skyscraper, and a Pokémon Center logo is printed in its lower right corner.

PokéPark was a Pokémon amusement park in Nagoya, at the Sasashima satellite site of the 2005 World Expo, open from 18 March to 25 September 2005.
